newsitem.title: USA: Citicorp Q2 higher, CEO sees challenges.
newsitem.headline: Citicorp Q2 higher, CEO sees challenges.

text.p: Citicorp Tuesday reported second-quarter net income rose to $1.02 billiion from $952 million a year ago and fully diluted earnings per share rose to $2.10 versus $1.86 a year ago.
In a statement, chairman and chief executive John Reed said while the results were good, "...global spread compression and our U.S. card business present challenges."

"Our assumption is that the highly competitive marketplace is a permanent reality," Reed said. He said the company would respond with "quality initiatives" to improve customer service and with "cost initiatives."

The year-over-year increase in second-quarter net income was eight percent, while per-share earnings were up 13 percent from a year ago. Average shares outstanding in the 1997 second quarter declined to 471.8 million from 492.1 million.
Citicorp said it repurchased 4.7 million shares of common stock for $524 million during the quarter.

Among business segments, the global consumer business which includes Citibanking, credit cards and the private bank had net income of $471 million, a three percent decline from $486 million a year ago. Adjusted revenue in the global consumer business rose six percent to $3.53 billion.

Citicorp said the decline in global consumer net income was priamrily due to a decline in U.S. bankcard earnings, which was partially offset by improved earnings in Citibanking, other cards businesses and its private bank.

Net income in cards worldwide fell 21 percent to $190 million. Citicorp said U.S. bankcards "continued to operate in a challenging environment characterized by competitive pressures and a weak credit climate."
Credit costs in U.S. cards rose to $683 million or 6.13 percent of average managed loans. The chargeoff rate in the first quarter was 5.91 percent versus 4.99 percent a year ago.
Citicorp said cards in force worldwide, including those issued by affiliates, totaled 63 million at the end of the second quarter, up four million from a year earlier.
In the global consumer business overall, credit costs rose to $922 million in the second quarter, up 21 percent from $762 million a year earlier.
Citibanking, which includes the branch network, had net income of $201 million in the second quarter, up 16 percent from a year ago.
The private bank had net income of $80 million in the second quarter, an increase of 10 percent from a year ago.

Citicorp said global corporate banking earned $665 million in the second quarter, up five percent from $636 million a year earlier. Income before taxes in global corporate banking rose 13 percent, to $824 million from $730 million. The difference between pre-tax and after-tax reflected a 19 percent effective tax rate in the quarter versus 13 percent a year ago.

Adjusted revenue in global corporate banking was $2.0 billion, up 11 percent from $1.8 billion a year earlier. Citicorp said $131 million of the increase was from its emerging markets business, and $68 million was from global relationship banking.
Emerging markets second quarter net income of $423 million declined $2 million from a year earlier. Citicorp cited an increase in the effective income tax rate, to 12 percent from five percent.
Net income from global relationship banking in North America, Europe and Japan was $242 million, up 15 percent from the 1996 second quarter.
Trading-related revenue of $243 million in global relationship banking rose $68 million from a year ago. The year-earlier period included a $60 million charge related to mortgage-backed securities.
Trading-related revenue overall was $511 million versus $427 million.
